clips.text: Your left hand just unbuttoned your shirt — while your right hand was still buttoning it. Only about 150 people have ever lived with a hand that has a mind of its own.
At breakfast, it grabs the hot pan. It pours the coffee on the table. Your right hand has to clean up after your left hand, every single morning.
In the mirror, it waves at strangers. It slaps your own face. Karen Byrne had to sit on her hand just to keep it still.
The cause is a broken bridge in your brain — the corpus callosum, about 200 million fibres joining two halves that can each hold their own will.
There is no cure. No pill rebuilds the bridge. You learn to live with a hand you cannot trust.
Your left hand just unbuttoned your shirt — while your right hand was still buttoning it. What would yours do first — help you, or fight you?
